evidence: Systematic gap across the Epic 46 agency-import feature: every state-changing mutation fires without an onError handler, isError branch, or user-visible toast/alert. When the server rejects the request (network / 403 / validation / rate-limit), the UI silently proceeds as if success — this is the same class of bug as the 2026-08-18-reality-web finding on inquiries/page.tsx cancel, but affects a broader surface (CRM + feed imports + branding + sync schedule).

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/import/CrmConnection.tsx:168-172 — handleDelete awaits deleteMutation.mutateAsync(connection.id) with no try/catch; grep of the whole file yields zero onError / isError / toast references. Line 215 syncMutation.mutate() and lines 372/391 test+create mutateAsync calls have the same gap.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/import/FeedImport.tsx:154-165 — handleTogglePause + handleDelete both await mutateAsync with no error catch; line 207 syncMutation.mutate() is pure fire-and-forget. Whole file also has zero onError / isError / toast.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/import/SyncSchedule.tsx:56-64 — handleSave awaits updateMutation.mutateAsync(...) then unconditionally setIsEditing(false); a failed save closes the edit form and the user sees the OLD schedule values re-rendered as though they saved.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/agency/AgencyBranding.tsx:78-95 — handleSave awaits updateBranding.mutateAsync({logo, coverImage, primaryColor, ...}) with no try/catch; a failed logo/cover upload becomes a silent unhandled promise rejection (browser-console only).

Fix vector: add a shared useMutationToast helper (or Sonner/react-hot-toast) and wire onError on every mutation hook — or at minimum an isError branch that surfaces the message in the existing card/modal.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/listings/ListingGrid.tsx — the PRIMARY listing-search-results grid has zero next-intl usage (no useTranslations import) on a sk/cs/de/en portal. Every other listings/* sibling (ContactForm, LayoutSections, ListingCard, ListingDetailContent, ListingFilters, PhotoGallery, SearchBar) DOES use useTranslations, so this component is a systemic gap in an otherwise localized directory.

and line 78 'Try adjusting your filters or search criteria to find more properties.' render raw English for every non-EN visitor whose search returns zero results — the empty-state on the highest-traffic route (/[locale]/listings).

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/auth/callback/page.tsx:83-91 — the SSO callback pulls `error` and `error_description` off the query string with searchParams.get(...) and passes them straight into setError(errorDescription || errorParam), which then renders as

{error}

on line 131. There is no allow-list of expected error codes, no length cap, and no scrubbing.

React JSX escaping prevents HTML/JS injection so this is NOT XSS, but an attacker who can hand a victim a link to /<locale>/auth/callback?error=x&error_description=Please+call+1-800-... renders arbitrary attacker-controlled body text under our origin, with our SSO chrome and our real 'Return Home' button — a page-shaped phishing surface hosted from the real reality-web SSO callback URL. Because the URL is legitimately linked from OAuth error redirects, users are trained to trust content on that route.

Additionally the same file (162 lines) has zero next-intl usage on the 4-locale portal: 'Login Failed' (L130), 'Return Home' (L133), 'Loading...' (L66), 'Completing login...' (L144), and the constructed 'Invalid state token. Please try logging in again.' (L106) all render English regardless of locale.

Fix vector: constrain error to a known enum ('access_denied', 'invalid_state', 'server_error', ...) and translate via useTranslations('auth.sso.error.<code>'); fall back to a single generic key when the code is unknown. Drop the raw error_description from the rendered UI (log it only). Wrap the remaining strings in t().
